idiom_name: tower Layer / axum middleware::from_fn around the Router
implementation_notes: Rust has no authentication in std; the de-facto realization is a tower Layer applied to the router (axum: middleware::from_fn_with_state), which is the enforcement checkpoint: it extracts the Authorization header, calls the verifier (jsonwebtoken, an OIDC client, a session store) and either inserts the principal into request extensions or returns 401. The mechanism is injected as state or a closure, and the classic interceptor object is unnecessary because tower services compose; a per-route extractor (a FromRequestParts implementation that requires the principal) is the declarative complement that makes the requirement visible in handler signatures and rejects at runtime if middleware is absent. Choose middleware for pipeline-wide policy, extractors when the protected set is route-specific.
pitfalls: The verifier usually performs async I/O; holding non-Send values across .await makes the middleware fail to compile on multi-threaded runtimes - keep state cheap and cloneable (Arc) instead.
Request extensions are typed: inserting one principal type and extracting another fails at runtime with a 500, so fix a single principal type shared by middleware and handlers.
